children: Kuwait is planning to construct a state-of-the-art biorefinery dedicated to producing sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), a local newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The project aligns with Kuwait’s efforts to adopt cleaner and more environmentally friendly energy solutions that contribute to reducing carbon emissions from the aviation sector and global air transport, the Arabic language daily Al-Seyassah said.

The project will be undertaken by the state-owned Kuwait National Petroleum Company (KNPC) which has recently merged Kuwait Integrated Petroleum Industries Company (KIPIC) in itself as part of oil sector restructuring.

“KNPC will conduct detailed and comprehensive feasibility studies exploring options for importing and blending sustainable fuels, as well as mechanisms for producing low-carbon aviation fuel locally,” the report said.

The technical studies are to be presented to KNPC’s Sustainability Committee before being submitted to the Sustainability Steering Committee at Kuwait Petroleum Corporation (KPC), which manages the country’s hydrocarbon sector.
“The aim is to establish a comprehensive roadmap and a clear timeline for implementing such pioneering environmental projects and achieving the desired goals by 2050,” the report said.
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
